{{Quote|Wayland is where Emperor Palpatine's secret toy-box was. All kinds of nasty dark side things on Wayland.|[[Vega Sepen]]|<ref name="EotV" />}}
'''Wayland''' was a lush, semi-tropical planet in the [[Outer Rim Territories/Legends|Outer Rim Territories]].

==History==
===Galactic Republic===
Wayland was discovered and colonized during the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic's]] second wave of expansion,<ref name="HttES" /> and served as a field hospital during the [[Mandalorian Wars]]. It was also the site of a factory for [[Lhosan Industries]]. At some point after the [[Third Galactic War]], a filing error removed all record of the planet from astrogation charts and planetary logs, so that years later, people living during the reign of [[Palpatine/Legends|Palpatine]] were unsure if "Wayland" was the planet's real name or a [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Imperial]] codename. The Human colonists quickly came into conflict with Wayland's indigenous sentient species, the "crystal-skinned" [[Myneyrsh]]i and the "lumpy armor-plated" [[Psadan]]s. In their early years, the colonists came to dominate the Myneryrshi and Psadans with Republic technology, but isolated over time, the colonists technologically regressed to the level of the indigenous species.

Centuries later, Wayland was rediscovered by the mad [[Geneticist/Legends|genetic]] [[Terrorist/Legends|terrorist]] [[Zeta Magnus]] who constructed an underground laboratory [[Mount Tantiss/Legends|facility]] there.<ref name="swcw">''[[SkyeWalkers: A Clone Wars Story]]''</ref> When Magnus pledged fealty to the [[Confederacy of Independent Systems/Legends|Confederacy of Independent Systems]], he granted [[Palpatine/Legends|Darth Sidious]] access to his Wayland facility. During the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]], the Wayland system was restricted by the Confederacy, and a [[Battle of Wayland (Clone Wars)|battle]] claiming the life of a [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]] was fought over the planet at some point.<ref name="Yoda: Dark Rendezvous">''[[Yoda: Dark Rendezvous]]''</ref> [[Dooku/Legends|Count Dooku]] would use Magnus' facility to experiment with [[dashta eel]] tissue samples for his [[JK-13 security droid]]s and for experimenting with cloning an [[Morgukai Shadow Army|army]] of [[Morgukai]] warriors. Darth Sidious determined the facility's isolation and uncharted nature made it ideal for a storehouse of arcane artifacts and secret technology.

===Imperial occupation===
{{Main|Occupation of Wayland}}
The [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]] had an [[Occupation of Wayland|occupation]] on the planet. They [[Slavery/Legends|enslaved]] the native [[Myneyrsh]]i, [[Psadan]]s, and their allies.<ref name="UAA" /> [[Emperor/Legends|Emperor]] Palpatine built his storehouse into Mount Tantiss in Wayland's northern hemisphere and placed a [[Dark Jedi/Legends|Dark Jedi]] as its [[Guardian of Mount Tantiss|Guardian]].<ref name="TTS">''[[The Thrawn Trilogy Sourcebook]]''</ref>

In [[3 BBY/Legends|3 BBY]], the Empire built a [[Imperial Research Station 61|research station]]. The research station, under the command of [[Commander/Legends|Commandant]], [[Colonel/Legends|Col.]] [[Milosh Muhrlein]], was suspected of selling experimental droids protocols and devices on the [[Black market/Legends|black market]]. This practice ended when [[Imperial Intelligence/Legends|Imperial Intelligence]] agent [[Jahan Cross]] and his droid [[IN-GA 44|IN-GA]] investigate and eliminated Muhrlein.<ref name="SW:AOTE,VI:IE" /> The Imperial occupation of Wayland ended shortly after the [[Battle of Endor/Legends|Battle of Endor]]<ref name="UAA" /> in [[4 ABY/Legends|4 ABY]].<ref name="TNEC">''[[The New Essential Chronology]]''</ref>

===Thrawn campaign===
{{Quote|The Emperor had a private storehouse. It was beneath a mountain on a world he called Wayland. It was where he kept all of his private mementos and souvenirs and odd bits of technology he thought might be useful someday.|[[Mara Jade Skywalker|Mara Jade]]|<ref name="TLC">''[[The Last Command]]''</ref>}}
In [[9 ABY/Legends|9 ABY]],<ref name="Five Years">''[[The Thrawn Trilogy Sourcebook]]'' states that the Guardian created his kingdom five years after the Battle of Endor. That battle took place in [[4 ABY/Legends|4 ABY]] per ''[[The New Essential Chronology]]''</ref> after five [[Standard year/Legends|years]] without Imperial contact in the wake of [[Battle of Endor/Legends|Palpatine's death]], the Guardian established a [[Mount Tantiss city|city]] he populated with Wayland's three native populations: [[Human/Legends|Humans]], [[Myneyrsh]]i, and the [[Psadan]]. [[Joruus C'baoth]], an insane [[Cloning/Legends|clone]] of the [[Jedi Master/Legends|Jedi Master]] [[Jorus C'baoth]] who had [[clone madness]], dueled with the Guardian later that year. The clone killed the Guardian and maintained the settlement himself.<ref name="TTS" /><ref name="Tantiss">{{CSWECite|I|337&ndash;338|Mount Tantiss}} This entry confirms objectively that C'baoth did kill the Guardian.</ref>

[[File:Wayland-TLC5.jpg|thumb|left|Imperial forces on Wayland.]]

C'baoth, hungry for power, established himself as the hand of justice on Wayland, installing a cruel, twisted [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]] code. The mad clone used his powers to bring a forced peace between the Humans, Psadans and Myneryrshi, culminating in a tense coexistence in a city southwest of Mount Tantiss.

Even later in [[9 ABY/Legends|9 ABY]], [[Grand Admiral/Legends|Grand Admiral]] [[Mitth'raw'nuruodo/Legends|Thrawn]] descended upon Wayland to claim the [[Cloaking device/Legends|cloaking shield]] technology and thousands of [[Spaarti cloning cylinder]]s that he used in his war against the [[New Republic/Legends|New Republic]]. The Mount Tantiss storehouse was eventually [[Assault on Mount Tantiss|destroyed]] by [[Lando Calrissian/Legends|Lando Calrissian]] and [[Chewbacca/Legends|Chewbacca]], and C'baoth killed by [[Mara Jade Skywalker|Mara Jade]].

After the destruction of Mount Tantiss, Wayland became a planet of particular interest to the New Republic as they took the planet away from the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]]. Researchers and [[New Republic Intelligence Service|New Republic Intelligence]] officers scoured the planet and ruins for clues to aid in their defeat of Imperial warlords, discovering evidence that would lead to the political fallout of [[Bothan/Legends|Bothan]] involvement in the destruction of [[Caamas/Legends|Caamas]]. The New Republic also relocated the [[Noghri/Legends|Noghri]] to the colony of [[New Nystao]] on Wayland to escape their collapsing home world of [[Honoghr/Legends|Honoghr]].

In [[14 ABY/Legends|14 ABY]], [[Corran Horn/Legends|Corran Horn]] was dispatched to Wayland to determine whether or not the [[Disciples of Ragnos]] had visited the planet to drain its [[The Force/Legends|Force]] energy.<ref name="JK:JA">''[[Star Wars: Jedi Knight: Jedi Academy]]''</ref>

In [[24 ABY/Legends|24 ABY]], the [[Book of Sith]] was rediscovered by [[Luke Skywalker/Legends|Luke Skywalker]] amid the ruins of the Emperor's storehouses at Mount Tantiss, after stumbling upon a chamber that, until that year remained hidden.<ref name="BOS">''[[Book of Sith: Secrets from the Dark Side]]''</ref>

===Yuuzhan Vong War===
In [[25 ABY/Legends|25 ABY]], Wayland acted as the site of the first interrogation of the [[Yuuzhan Vong]] priestess [[Elan]] and her familiar [[Vergere]], but due to an [[Raid on Wayland (25 ABY)|attack]] by Yuuzhan Vong forces they were relocated. It also served as a safe world for New Republic personnel during the early stages of the [[Yuuzhan Vong War]]. Wayland's secrecy was eventually disrupted by [[Elan]], who transmitted its location to the Vong with a hidden [[villip]]. Despite the harshness of the attack, there were few casualties among the Noghri in residence.<ref name="AoCI:HT" /><ref name="db" />

The Yuuzhan Vong later brutally subjugated Wayland, terraformed it to serve as an organic weaponry breeding ground and destroyed much of the planet's crust and mantle with [[Chom-Vrone]].<ref name="EotV" /> [[Amphistaff]]s from Wayland were also found among [[Peace Brigade]] cargo during the late stages of the war.<ref name="Rebirth">''[[The New Jedi Order: Edge of Victory II: Rebirth]]''</ref> The New Republic later [[Raid on Wayland (28 ABY)|raided]] the world in order to train new recruits in combat in preparation for the decisive [[Battle of Ebaq]].<ref name="Destiny's Way">''[[The New Jedi Order: Destiny's Way]]''</ref>

===Legacy era===
Wayland was later one of the first subjects of the [[Ossus Project]], and was also one of the first failures of that project.<ref name="Legacy 2006 44">[[Legacy (2006) 44|''Legacy'' (2006) 44]]</ref> By the time of the [[Second Imperial Civil War]], the planet had been, for all intents and purposes, quarantined.

==Behind the scenes==
Despite Wayland's apparently unknown nature, several passages in the novel ''[[Yoda: Dark Rendezvous]]'' reference the planet directly, including mention of a battle occurring over the world and the [[Confederacy of Independent Systems/Legends|Confederacy of Independent Systems]] blockading it.

Additionally, in the [[2006]] video game ''[[Star Wars: Empire at War]]'', [[Raymus Antilles/Legends|Raymus Antilles]] sends [[C-3PO/Legends|C-3PO]] and [[R2-D2/Legends|R2-D2]] to the planet. However, in the [[1991]] novel ''[[Heir to the Empire]]'', which takes place long after the game in [[9 ABY/Legends|9 ABY]], no-one seems to have any knowledge of the existence of Wayland, except for certain high-ranking Imperial officials.
